Subject: Your renewal is coming up — quick proposal inside

Hi Andrés,

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to reach out personally because your contract with us is up for renewal on June 15th, and based on the conversations our team has had with yours over the past quarter, I think there's a meaningful opportunity to expand the partnership.

Three things on my mind:

1. Your team has driven a 40% increase in API call volume over the last six months — well beyond what your current tier supports. We should level you up before you hit the ceiling.

2. The new analytics dashboard we shipped in Q1 isn't available on your plan, but your operations team would get real value from it. Happy to comp you a 90-day trial as part of the renewal.

3. I'd like to lock in your current per-seat rate for another two years before the price increase takes effect in September.

Could you spare 20 minutes next week to walk through this together? I'm flexible Tuesday through Thursday.

Looking forward to it.

Best,
Claire Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Customer Success

# Translation: Customer success renewal email (EN → ES)

## Register & audience analysis
This is a B2B customer success email to a senior executive (Director of Operations) at a paying enterprise client in Colombia. I used **usted** throughout. Colombian business culture leans formal, and *usted* is safe even in a warm relationship. The English is friendly but businesslike ("Hi Andrés", "Happy to comp you"). I kept that warmth but raised the formality slightly, since a $180K renewal shouldn't read as casual. The Spanish is neutral Latin American and natural for Colombian readers.

## Translation

**Asunto:** Renovación de su contrato: una propuesta breve

Buenos días, Andrés:

Espero que se encuentre muy bien. Quise escribirle personalmente porque su contrato con nosotros se renueva el 15 de junio y, a partir de las conversaciones que nuestros equipos han sostenido durante el último trimestre, considero que existe una oportunidad significativa para ampliar nuestra alianza.

Hay tres puntos que quisiera plantearle:

1. Su equipo ha impulsado un aumento del 40 % en el volumen de llamadas a la API durante los últimos seis meses, muy por encima de lo que admite su nivel actual. Convendría migrar su cuenta a un nivel superior antes de que alcancen el límite.

2. El nuevo panel de analítica que lanzamos en el primer trimestre no está incluido en su plan, pero su equipo de operaciones le sacaría un gran provecho. Con gusto le ofrecemos una prueba de cortesía de 90 días como parte de la renovación.

3. Me gustaría asegurarle su tarifa actual por usuario durante dos años más, antes de que entre en vigor el aumento de precios en septiembre.

¿Podría dedicarnos 20 minutos la próxima semana para revisar esto juntos? Tengo disponibilidad de martes a jueves.

Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.

Cordialmente,

Claire Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Customer Success

## Glossary of key terms

| Source | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| renewal | renovación | Standard term |
| partnership | alianza | Better than *asociación*, which can sound legal or corporate |
| API call volume | volumen de llamadas a la API | "API" stays in English, as is standard in LatAm tech |
| tier | nivel | Kept separate from "plan", as in the source |
| plan | plan | — |
| analytics dashboard | panel de analítica | *Dashboard* is also common in Colombian SaaS; *panel* is more polished |
| comp (a trial) | prueba de cortesía | Says the trial is a goodwill gesture, which a plain "free trial" would lose |
| per-seat rate | tarifa por usuario | *Por puesto* would be a calque; *por licencia* also works |
| lock in | asegurarle | Means "secure it for you"; *congelar* is an option if you want to stress a price freeze |

## Translator's notes

1. **"Hi Andrés," → "Buenos días, Andrés:"**: A literal "Hola Andrés" is too casual for this relationship. "Estimado Andrés:" is the other standard option. "Buenos días" is very common in Colombian business email. It's also gender-neutral, so the email works without me assuming anything from the name. The colon after the greeting is standard in Spanish letters.
2. **"Looking forward to it." → "Quedo a la espera de su respuesta."**: This is the usual formal sign-off. I didn't use "Quedo atenta/atento" because it's gendered and would assume Claire's gender.
3. **Signature title kept in English**: English job titles are common in LatAm SaaS. If you want it in Spanish, it would be *Ejecutiva de Cuentas Sénior* or *Ejecutivo de Cuentas Sénior*, depending on how Claire refers to herself.
4. **"We should level you up before you hit the ceiling"**: This is informal English, so I rewrote it more formally as "Convendría migrar su cuenta a un nivel superior antes de que alcancen el límite." The meaning is the same: upgrade before they hit the cap.
5. **"40 %"**: I added a space before the % sign, following RAE style. "40%" without the space is also common in Colombia, so either is fine.
6. **Date check**: Today is October 26, 2026. "June 15th" and "September" don't state a year, and "Q1" may need checking too. The September price increase should still be in the future, and it should land after the June renewal. Adding years (for example, "15 de junio de 2027") would avoid any ambiguity.

# Translation: Customer success renewal email (EN → ES)

## Register & audience analysis
This is a B2B customer success email about renewing and expanding a $180K contract. The reader is a Director of Operations at a Colombian logistics company. I used **usted** throughout. Colombian business culture keeps usted in professional relationships even when people know each other well, so tú would come across as too familiar. The English is warm and fairly casual ("level you up," "hit the ceiling," "three things on my mind"). I kept the warmth but raised the tone slightly to fit Colombian business email. The content stays the same: nothing is added or softened.

## Translation

**Asunto:** Se acerca su renovación: una breve propuesta

Estimado Andrés:

Espero que se encuentre muy bien. Quise escribirle personalmente porque la renovación de su contrato con nosotros está prevista para el 15 de junio y, a partir de las conversaciones que nuestros equipos han sostenido durante el último trimestre, creo que existe una oportunidad importante para ampliar nuestra alianza.

Quisiera plantearle tres puntos:

1. En los últimos seis meses, su equipo ha impulsado un aumento del 40 % en el volumen de llamadas a la API, muy por encima de lo que cubre su plan actual. Conviene que pasemos a un plan superior antes de que alcancen el límite.

2. El nuevo panel de analítica que lanzamos en el primer trimestre no está incluido en su plan, pero sería de gran valor para su equipo de operaciones. Con gusto podemos ofrecerle una prueba sin costo de 90 días como parte de la renovación.

3. Me gustaría asegurar su tarifa actual por usuario durante dos años más, antes de que entre en vigor el aumento de precios en septiembre.

¿Podría reservar 20 minutos la próxima semana para revisarlo juntos? Tengo disponibilidad de martes a jueves.

Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.

Cordialmente,
Claire Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Customer Success

## Glossary of key terms

| Source | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| renewal | renovación | Standard term. |
| partnership | alianza | Better than *sociedad*, which suggests a legal partnership. |
| API call volume | volumen de llamadas a la API | "API" stays in English, which is standard in LatAm tech. It takes the feminine article (*la API*). |
| tier / plan | plan | I used one word for both, because *nivel* sounds odd in a commercial context. |
| level you up | pasar a un plan superior | Plain business wording in place of the gaming-style slang. |
| analytics dashboard | panel de analítica | Neutral LatAm. *Dashboard* also works if your product UI uses it. |
| comp you a trial | ofrecerle una prueba sin costo | "Comp" has no direct equivalent. *Sin costo* is more natural in Colombia than *gratuita* for B2B. |
| per-seat rate | tarifa por usuario | "Seat" doesn't carry over. *Por licencia* is an alternative if your contracts use that word. |
| Q1 | primer trimestre | Abbreviations like "T1" or "Q1" read as jargon in Spanish prose. |

## Translator's notes

1. **The dates are in the past. Please check before sending.** Today is 26 October 2026. The renewal date (15 June) and the price increase ("in September") have both already passed this year. If this is a reused template, or it's meant for 2027, update the dates. Adding the year would also help, for example *15 de junio de 2027*.
2. **Signer's gender.** Several natural Spanish closings and titles depend on the writer's gender: *Quedo atento/atenta*, *Ejecutivo/Ejecutiva Sénior de Cuentas*. I didn't want to assume, so I used the gender-neutral *Quedo a la espera de su respuesta* and kept the job title in English, which is common in signatures at multinational companies. If you'd like a Spanish title, confirm which form Claire uses, e.g. *Ejecutiva Sénior de Cuentas, Éxito del Cliente*.
3. **"Hi Andrés" → "Estimado Andrés:"** Spanish letter convention puts a colon after the greeting. *Apreciado Andrés:* is also very common in Colombia and a little warmer. Either works.
4. **"40 %"** follows the RAE recommendation of a space before %. Many LatAm companies write "40%" instead. Use whatever your house style is.
5. **"I hope this email finds you well"** is rendered as *Espero que se encuentre muy bien*, the natural Spanish equivalent. A literal translation would be a calque.
6. **"Looking forward to it"** has no tidy formal equivalent. *Quedo a la espera de su respuesta* is the standard formal closing.
